conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I'll be your doctor during this stay. You're here because of abdominal pain, right?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it’s the same kind of pain I’ve had before with pancreatitis. It started two nights ago—epigastric, radiating to my back, really sharp.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. And you’ve been vomiting too?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes, non-stop since it started. Now it’s just dry heaving. I can’t keep anything down, not even my meds.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. We’ll keep you NPO for now—no food or drink by mouth—to let your pancreas rest.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. But I did manage to take my Coumadin and lisinopril earlier. Should I keep trying?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: No, don’t try to take anything by mouth right now. We’ll give your meds through your IV or J-tube if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. My port was placed a few days ago—right side chest. It’s not painful or red.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good, I see the site—it looks clean. We’ll use that for your IV meds and labs.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had over 30 admissions for this. Is this another flare?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, it looks like an acute flare of your chronic pancreatitis. Your lipase is normal, but your symptoms and history are classic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my triglycerides? I know they were high last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: They’re elevated at 414, which can contribute to flares. But no imaging is needed—we’re managing based on your typical pattern.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. What about pain control? I need something strong.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re starting your usual IV regimen: Dilaudid every two hours, Ketorolac, and Phenergan for nausea.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. And fluids?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, IV fluids at 125 mL/hour to keep you hydrated while you’re NPO.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: My blood pressure’s been high. Is that a concern?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s 176/114 now—likely due to pain. We’ve held your lisinopril since you’re not eating, but we’ll restart it when you can take pills.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my Coumadin? I’m on it for DVT history.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your INR was low at 1.1 on admission, so we’ve started Lovenox injections to bridge you until you can take Coumadin again safely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I understand. I’ve had clots before—left arm and now right IJ.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, and with your port and history, we’ll keep you on anticoagulation long-term.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How’s the pain today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A little better. Still nauseous, but not vomiting as much.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s progress. We’ll keep you NPO a bit longer, but we’ll start advancing your diet tomorrow if you keep improving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I have ice chips or water?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not yet. We want to be sure your gut is ready. We’ll try clear liquids tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. My blood pressure still high?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s coming down—158/98 this morning. As your pain improves, it should normalize.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing well. We’re going to try clear liquids today—start with broth and apple juice.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great! Can I also restart my amitriptyline and methadone?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’ll restart those by mouth. We’ve increased your lisinopril to 40 mg daily for now to help with BP.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Why increase it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Because your BP has been persistently elevated. We’ll lower it back to 10 mg once it’s stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You tolerated the clear liquids. Today, we’ll advance to soft foods—mashed potatoes, applesauce.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Perfect. And my Coumadin? Can I restart it?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re restarting it today. You’ll stay on both Coumadin and Lovenox until your INR is therapeutic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: What’s my INR today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s 1.6—still subtherapeutic. We’ll check again in two days.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re eating regular food now and pain is much better. We’re switching your pain meds to oral Dilaudid.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can I take it as needed?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, one tablet every three hours as needed. We’ll send some home with you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my amitriptyline? I was on 25 mg at night.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve increased it to 75 mg nightly. It helps with nerve pain and mood.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your INR is still 1.6. We’re adjusting your Coumadin dose to 7.5 mg daily.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I keep the Lovenox too?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, once daily 100 mg until your INR is above 2 for 24 hours. Then you can stop the shots.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. And when do I go home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: If all goes well, probably in two to three days. We’ll check your labs tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs look stable. Pain is controlled, you’re eating well. We’re planning discharge tomorrow.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Great. What about my meds at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll go home on your regular meds. Coumadin at 7.5 mg daily, Lovenox once a day until your INR is therapeutic.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the dose change?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll take 10 mg tonight, then 7.5 mg daily after that. Your INR needs to be checked soon after discharge.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And lisinopril?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Back to your usual 10 mg daily. Your BP is much better—145/99 this morning.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: All set for discharge tomorrow. You’re doing really well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Can someone help me with the Lovenox injections at home?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, a nurse will come to your home to assist until your INR is stable.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And follow-up?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll see your primary doctor and the anticoagulation clinic. They’ll manage your INR checks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re cleared to go home. Keep taking your meds as discussed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So, Coumadin 10 mg tonight, then 7.5 mg daily, and Lovenox until INR is good?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. And call if you have severe pain, vomiting, or signs of bleeding.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: One more thing—my anemia. Labs were low again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your hemoglobin is 9.3. It’s likely anemia of chronic disease from your pancreatitis. No transfusion needed now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Should I take iron?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Not right now. Your levels are stable. We’ll monitor it at your follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my migraines?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You can resume your butalbital as needed. Avoid triggers and keep a headache diary.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been anxious this stay. Any advice?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Keep taking your amitriptyline. It helps with both pain and mood. Consider talking to a counselor if anxiety worsens.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re doing great. Just take it slow at home and call with any concerns.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. I’m ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: The discharge team will bring your prescriptions and instructions shortly.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I’ll pack up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’ll see you in the clinic soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you, Dr. Lee.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Have a safe trip home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll be in touch with your PCP to coordinate care.
